100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On July 25, 1926, the British Empire faced turmoil as a general strike in the coal industry threatened to spread, potentially paralyzing the nation's economy. Meanwhile, in the United States, President Calvin Coolidge continued his campaign for economic prosperity, emphasizing the importance of reduced government intervention. In international affairs, tensions rose in the Far East as Japan and China grappled with territorial disputes, raising concerns among Western powers.
